html:
St George's, at the east end of Bermuda, was founded in 1612 by the first English settlers sent after the wreck of the Sea Venture. It is the oldest English town in the Americas still lived in.

It was Bermuda's capital until 1815, when the government moved to Hamilton. Its forts, built over three centuries, guarded the narrow channel into the harbour; St Peter's Church is among the oldest Anglican churches outside the British Isles.

During the American Civil War, Confederate blockade runners used the port. The town and its forts became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000. It was run in its first decades by the Somers Isles Company for the English crown.
